newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan Ag says hot, dry weather yield threat.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan Ag says hot, dry weather yield threat.

text.p: Crop yield prospects continued to be threatened by hot, dry weather which advanced crop growth rapidly, Saskatchewan Agriculture said in its report.

Eighty-five percent of spring cereals were at or past the dough stage compared to the five-year average of 42 percent. Eighty percent of flax reached or past the boll stage versus the average 38 percent. Ninety percent of canola was at or beyond the podding stage compared to the average 60 percent.
Swathing and combining of fall cereals was underway with the southern grainbelt most advanced. Diamondback moths and Bertha armyworms were seen south of the TransCanada Highway.
The southern grainbelt saw hot and dry weather with an average one mm of rain. Wind damage was reported in the southeast and southwest. Hail damage was seen in the southwest.
Central Saskatchewan saw dry and hot weather with an average one mm of rain. Heat and drought stress were widely reported as a source of crop damage.

Northern grainbelt crops saw hot and dry weather with an average six mm (0.2 inch) of rain. Drought and heat stress damaged crops across the region. Localized wind damage was seen as was hail around Prince Albert and North Battleford.
